global-marketplace-audit.title: Technical SEO Audit & Optimization for a Luxury Marketplace
global-marketplace-audit.summary: Technical SEO for a large U.S. luxury marketplace on a custom platform: search intent realigned across thousands of templated pages, canonical and 404 errors fixed, URL structure planned for the new platform. Organic traffic up 6% to 562.8K monthly visits.
global-marketplace-audit.challenge: On a site with thousands of generated pages, every problem repeats at scale. The audit found that many pages did not match the intent of the people searching for them, and that technical errors were wasting Google's crawling.
global-marketplace-audit.approach: Executed a multi-phase technical audit. Phase 1 focused on metadata optimization (titles/H1 consistency). Phase 2 addressed site health by fixing 'no response' errors and implementing self-referencing canonicals on listing detail pages. Phase 3 involved updating Schema.org markup and optimizing internal linking equity.

results.0: Organic Traffic +6% (562.8K monthly visits - US Data)
results.1: Keyword Visibility +3.3% (281.4K ranked keywords - US Data)

gallery_alts.0: Organic traffic and keyword trend, 2024 to 2025 (US data)
gallery_alts.1: SEO dashboard: 562.8K organic traffic and 281.4K ranked keywords (US data)
gallery_alts.2: Google Search Console, 16 months: 5.99M clicks and 214M impressions

global-marketplace-audit.seo_title: Technical SEO Case Study: Large Luxury Marketplace
global-marketplace-audit.context: The client is a large luxury marketplace whose main market is the United States. The site already had serious search traffic: Google Search Console showed 5.99 million clicks and 214 million impressions over 16 months. It does not run on a standard CMS: pages are generated from templates, formulas and a dynamic structure, so one change applies to thousands of pages at once. I directed the technical SEO as the only SEO specialist at a digital marketing agency, and coordinated every change with the agency's developers. It was the largest project I have worked on.

problems.title: Search intent not targeted on most pages
problems.desc: Many pages were not aimed at what searchers actually wanted: titles, headings and content did not match the intent behind the queries they appeared for.

problems.title: Titles and H1s that did not agree
problems.desc: On core pages, the title tag and the H1 heading described the page in different ways, sending Google mixed signals.

problems.title: Canonical errors and 404s
problems.desc: Google Search Console reported canonical issues, and the crawl found 404 pages and URLs with no response. Listing pages did not declare themselves as the main version of their URL, so Google had to guess which version to rank.

problems.title: Other crawl issues and outdated structured data
problems.desc: Screaming Frog surfaced broken internal links and other issues, and the Schema.org markup needed updating.

steps.title: Search intent, at template level
steps.desc: I realigned titles, H1s and on-page content with search intent. Because pages are generated from templates and formulas, each fix applied to thousands of pages.

steps.title: Search Console and crawl errors
steps.desc: I fixed most of the issues reported in Google Search Console, including canonical errors and 404s, plus the issues found with Screaming Frog. Listing detail pages now carry a self-referencing canonical.

steps.title: Structured data and internal links
steps.desc: I updated the Schema.org markup and reworked internal linking so more link value flows to the most important pages.

steps.title: URL structure for the new platform
steps.desc: The client was building a new version of the platform. I wrote a detailed document recommending the URL structure to use, comparing flat and nested (structured) URLs, so the new version would launch on a sound base.

steps.title: Working with the developers
steps.desc: Since the site has no CMS, every change went through the agency's development team, and I coordinated each one with them.

steps.title: Measurement
steps.desc: Organic traffic and ranked keywords were tracked in Semrush on U.S. data, alongside Google Search Console.

lessons: On a templated site, fix the template, not the page. One corrected formula fixes every page built from it, which is how thousands of pages were improved.
Plan the URL structure before a platform rebuild. Changing URLs after launch means redirects, lost signals and months of recovery.
Small percentages are big numbers at this size. A 6% gain on a site at 562.8K monthly organic visits is roughly 30,000 more visits a month.

uk-compliance-service-audit.seo_title: Local SEO and CRO Case Study: UK Service Business
uk-compliance-service-audit.context: The client is a UK service business in the London market. Its main service is landlord safety compliance, which property owners search for when they need a certificate or an inspection. From January to May 2025 I worked with the business full-time, remotely, and handled all its local SEO, plus the Google Ads audit. The site had traffic on its key pages, but too few of those visitors became enquiries, and the business did not appear in the local map results.

problems.title: 1,170 crawled pages with “no response” errors
problems.desc: A crawl returned 1,170 pages with no response. That much noise wastes Google's crawling and hides the pages that should rank.

problems.title: Missing H1s and duplicate meta descriptions
problems.desc: Key pages had no H1 heading, and many pages shared the same meta description, so neither Google nor searchers could tell the pages apart.

problems.title: Slow on mobile
problems.desc: Mobile PageSpeed was 66. Most people searching for a local service do it on a phone, and a slow page loses them before they read the offer.

problems.title: Invisible in the map results
problems.desc: The business did not show in the local map pack for its services in London.

steps.title: Google Ads audit
steps.desc: Auditing the Google Ads account, I found that the landing page receiving the paid traffic was poorly designed and not built to convert. A campaign from 23 February to 3 April 2025 brought 625 clicks and 45 conversions, a conversion rate of about 7%.

steps.title: A redesigned landing page
steps.desc: I worked with the developer to redesign that page with clear trust signals. Its mobile PageSpeed went from 66 to 93, desktop from 90 to 97, and conversions on it more than doubled in the first month.

steps.title: Keyword research and a keyword map
steps.desc: I researched keywords in Semrush and other tools, and mapped primary, secondary and question keywords for the main service page.

steps.title: Metadata on every page
steps.desc: I rewrote the meta titles and descriptions of every page in Rank Math, and optimized 26 core pages and 20 existing blog posts.

steps.title: Weekly articles
steps.desc: I published a new article every week, targeting long-tail searches, with 10 new articles in the period covered here.

steps.title: Technical fixes
steps.desc: Using Screaming Frog and Google Search Console, I fixed more than 10 critical issues, including blocked pages and broken links.

steps.title: Local SEO
steps.desc: I optimized the Google Business Profile and built citations and backlinks, to make the business visible in the London map results.

lessons: When a page gets traffic but few enquiries, start with the page, not with more traffic. Here, a redesigned landing page doubled conversions in its first month.
Paid and organic search help each other. The Google Ads audit is what revealed the weak landing page, and the fix improved results for both.
Local SEO is many small jobs done every week: metadata, articles, profile, citations and links. Consistency is what makes it work.

saas-digital-launch.tags: SEO Strategy • Web Design • Marketing Automation
saas-digital-launch.challenge: Starting from nothing has one advantage: the structure can be right from day one. The risk is launching a site that looks good but that Google cannot read and that lets interested visitors leave without a trace.
saas-digital-launch.approach: Acting as the SEO & Digital Marketing Consultant, I developed a fully responsive website using a no-code builder. Implemented a comprehensive SEO strategy, structuring navigation for user intent. Integrated Gist for chatbot and email automation workflows to nurture leads. Established a multi-channel social presence on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.

saas-digital-launch.seo_title: SaaS Launch Case Study: Website, SEO and Lead Automation
saas-digital-launch.context: The client was a new inventory management brand with no website, no search presence and no way to collect leads. From January to May 2025 I worked with them part-time and owned the whole digital marketing side, not only SEO: the website, search, CRM and automation, social media and the content plan for the launch.

problems.title: No website
problems.desc: The brand needed a mobile-responsive site, built on a no-code builder.

problems.title: No SEO foundation
problems.desc: Pages, navigation and on-page elements had to be planned around how buyers search for inventory software, before any content was written.

problems.title: No lead capture
problems.desc: Early visitors had no way to ask questions or leave their details, so interest from launch would be lost.

steps.title: The website, with a freelance developer
steps.desc: A freelance developer built the site on a no-code builder, and I directed the work: structure, pages, what to do and what to avoid for SEO. The site went through two design versions, a light one at first and then a dark one.

steps.title: Technical and on-page SEO
steps.desc: I handled all the SEO: the technical setup, navigation planned around user intent so each main page answers one type of search, and the on-page work on every page.

steps.title: Link building plan
steps.desc: I planned the link building for after the launch, so the new domain could start earning authority.

steps.title: CRM, chat and email automation
steps.desc: I set up the CRM and Gist for live chat and email automation, so visitors could ask questions on the site and leads received follow-up emails automatically.

steps.title: Social media and launch content
steps.desc: I created the brand's Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn accounts, planned the content for the launch, made visuals in Canva and set up Google Analytics.

lessons: Plan the site structure before the design. Navigation built around search intent is far easier to rank than pages reorganized after launch.
When a developer builds the site, give SEO instructions before the build starts, not after. Fixing structure later costs more than getting it right the first time.
Capture leads before you have traffic. A chat widget and an email sequence from day one mean early visitors are not lost.

premium-medspa-seo-audit.title: Technical SEO Audit & Local Optimization for U.S.-Based Medical Spa
premium-medspa-seo-audit.summary: A U.S. medical spa's SEO titles were missing from its HTML because two SEO plugins clashed, and its canonicals pointed to a development domain. I fixed both, rewrote titles and descriptions from new keyword research and optimized images. Traffic and CTR rose in the following weeks.
premium-medspa-seo-audit.tags: Technical SEO • Local SEO • Site Audit
premium-medspa-seo-audit.challenge: Poor visibility usually points to content or links. Here, the first checks found something more basic: Google was not receiving the right signals from the pages at all.
premium-medspa-seo-audit.approach: Conducted a comprehensive SEO audit covering technical, on-page, and local SEO factors. Built an SEO Implementation Tracking Sheet to organize all optimizations and monitor progress. Resolved the metadata visibility issue by deactivating RankMath and maintaining Yoast SEO as the single source of truth. Fixed all canonical tag errors to ensure each page properly referenced its authoritative URL. Drafted optimized titles, meta descriptions, and heading structures for service and location pages. Developed a detailed Local SEO Strategy covering on-page optimization, local citations, link building, and content strategy.

results.1: Every canonical tag pointing to the live URL
results.2: Traffic and click-through rate rising in the weeks after the changes
results.3: Local SEO roadmap delivered for the next phase

premium-medspa-seo-audit.seo_title: Technical and Local SEO Case Study: U.S. Medical Spa
premium-medspa-seo-audit.context: The client is a medical spa in the United States offering premium treatments. Despite the quality of its services, the website had poor visibility in Google. A dashboard snapshot from the project shows 83 organic visits, 212 ranking keywords and an Authority Score of 18. I handled the SEO as the only SEO specialist at a digital marketing agency.

problems.title: SEO titles and descriptions missing from the HTML
problems.desc: Two SEO plugins, Rank Math and Yoast SEO, were active at the same time. The conflict meant the titles and meta descriptions written for the pages did not appear in the HTML source that Google reads.

problems.title: Canonical tags pointing to the wrong place
problems.desc: Some canonical tags referenced the wrong URL, and others pointed to a local development domain instead of the live site. In effect, the site was telling Google that its real pages lived somewhere else.

problems.title: Service pages that could not rank
problems.desc: Together, these issues stopped Google from properly crawling, indexing and ranking the service pages.

steps.title: Full audit
steps.desc: I audited the technical, on-page and local SEO factors, and built an SEO implementation tracking sheet to organize every change and follow its progress.

steps.title: One SEO plugin
steps.desc: I deactivated Rank Math and kept Yoast SEO as the single source of SEO settings. The titles and meta descriptions appeared in the HTML again.

steps.title: Canonicals corrected
steps.desc: I fixed every canonical tag so that each page points to its own live URL.

steps.title: Keyword research from scratch
steps.desc: I redid the keyword research for the services and locations, so the new titles and descriptions would target what people actually search for.

steps.title: New titles, descriptions and headings
steps.desc: I wrote new titles, meta descriptions and heading structures for the service and location pages, and they went live after the client approved them.

steps.title: Image optimization
steps.desc: I converted the images to WebP, which makes pages lighter and faster, and added descriptive alt text so Google understands what each image shows.

steps.title: Local SEO strategy
steps.desc: I wrote a local SEO strategy covering on-page optimization, local citations, link building and content.

lessons: Never run two SEO plugins at once. They overwrite each other's output, and the result can be pages with no title or description at all.
Check canonical tags after any move from a staging or development site. Canonicals that still point to the old domain are a common and costly leftover.

Fix the signals before writing more content. New pages will not help while Google receives the wrong URL or no title for the pages you already have. Here, traffic and clicks started rising within weeks of the fixes, without a single new page.
premium-medspa-seo-audit.seo_description: A U.S. medical spa lost its SEO titles to a plugin conflict and its canonicals pointed to a dev domain. How the audit fixed both and lifted CTR.

national-sports-org.seo_title: SEO Content Case Study: National Sports Federation
national-sports-org.seo_description: Keyword research, SEO content, titles and meta descriptions for three pages of a national sports federation's website, including its partners page.
national-sports-org.role: Sole SEO specialist at a digital marketing agency
national-sports-org.context: The client is a national sports federation, served by the digital marketing agency where I was the only SEO specialist. My part of this project was deliberately small: the federation's partners page and two other pages of its website.

steps.title: Keyword research for each page
steps.desc: I researched the searches each page should answer, including the names and terms people use when they look for the federation's partners.

steps.title: Content optimization
steps.desc: I optimized the content of the three pages around those keywords, so each page states its topic clearly in the words people search with.

steps.title: Titles, descriptions and on-page elements
steps.desc: I wrote new SEO titles and meta descriptions and handled the other on-page elements, so the pages present themselves well in Google's results.

lessons: Partners pages are easy to overlook, yet people search for an organization's sponsors and partners by name. A clear, well-titled page can capture those searches.
Do the keyword research before writing. It shows which words people really use, which are often different from an organization's official terms.
A small scope is still worth doing properly. A few pages with the right keywords, content and metadata are better than many pages touched lightly.

law-firm-local-seo.title: Local SEO for a Personal Injury Law Firm in Michigan
law-firm-local-seo.summary: Local SEO for a personal injury law firm in Michigan: page fixes, CTR work on high-impression pages, orphan pages linked, citations audited and a suspended Google Business Profile recovered. 30% more qualified leads from local search.
law-firm-local-seo.tags: Local SEO • Google Business Profile • On-Page SEO
law-firm-local-seo.challenge: The firm wanted more clients from local search in its practice area. The site had pages with technical and on-page problems, pages Google was showing but few people clicked, and pages with no internal links at all. In the middle of the project, a bigger problem arrived: the firm's main Google Business Profile was suspended.
law-firm-local-seo.approach: I restructured the site into clear practice area sections. I optimized the on-page content for local searches (city plus practice area) and built quality local citations.

results.0: 30% more qualified leads from local search
results.1: First-page rankings for “city + personal injury” searches
results.2: Main Google Business Profile recovered after a suspension

law-firm-local-seo.seo_title: Personal Injury Law Firm SEO Case Study: Michigan
law-firm-local-seo.context: The client is a personal injury law firm in Michigan. Personal injury is one of the most competitive areas in legal search: people searching for a lawyer after an accident usually call one of the first firms they see, so ranking on page one for “city plus personal injury lawyer” searches makes a direct difference to new cases. I worked on this account as the only SEO specialist at a digital marketing agency.

problems.title: Pages with errors and weak on-page signals
problems.desc: The site audit found pages with technical and on-page problems that held them back.

problems.title: High impressions, low clicks
problems.desc: Search Console showed queries and pages with many impressions but poor positions and few clicks. Google already associated these pages with the right searches; they were not convincing enough to rank higher or earn the click.

problems.title: Orphan pages
problems.desc: Some pages had no internal links pointing to them. Google finds pages mostly by following links, so an orphan page is hard to discover and rarely ranks.

problems.title: A suspended Google Business Profile
problems.desc: The firm's main profile was suspended. For a local law firm, that profile is what appears in the map results, so the suspension cut off one of its most important sources of calls. The team was understandably alarmed.

steps.title: Fixing the problem pages
steps.desc: I went through the site, fixed the pages that had problems, and restructured the content into clear practice area sections so each area had a page strong enough to rank.

steps.title: CTR work on high-impression pages
steps.desc: Using Search Console, I picked the pages and queries with the most impressions and the weakest positions, and optimized their titles, descriptions and content to match what those searchers wanted.

steps.title: Orphan pages and internal links
steps.desc: I audited the site for orphan pages and linked every page from relevant content, so all pages are connected and discoverable by Google.

steps.title: Blog content
steps.desc: I published blog posts targeting questions potential clients search for.

steps.title: Citation audit
steps.desc: Using Local Falcon and other local SEO tools, I audited the firm's existing citations and local rankings, to check that its name, address and phone number were consistent and to see where it ranked across the area.

steps.title: Recovering the Google Business Profile
steps.desc: When the main profile was suspended, I gave the firm a clear plan: what to do, what to avoid while the profile was down, and how to request reinstatement. The profile was recovered.

lessons: Start with the pages Google already shows. Pages with many impressions and poor positions are the fastest wins, because Google has already connected them to the right searches.
Check for orphan pages. A page with no internal links can be well written and still never rank, because Google rarely finds it.

If your Google Business Profile is suspended, do not panic and do not create a new one. Follow the reinstatement process carefully: a rushed reaction can make it harder to get the original profile back.

moroccan-b2b-seo.title: On-Page SEO Optimization for a Moroccan B2B Website
moroccan-b2b-seo.summary: Freelance on-page SEO for a Moroccan B2B website whose pages brought no traffic: keywords retargeted from Search Console and competitor data, titles and descriptions rewritten, schema added. Clicks from 32 to 74 in 3 months, CTR from 0.7% to 1.6%.
moroccan-b2b-seo.tags: On-Page SEO • CTR Optimization • Internal Linking
moroccan-b2b-seo.challenge: The goal was to bring more qualified visitors without creating new pages. Search Console showed why the pages were not working: they were not targeting the right keywords.
moroccan-b2b-seo.approach: I improved keyword targeting within homepage content and rewrote meta titles/descriptions to align with search intent. I also improved page clarity and strengthened internal linking structure.
moroccan-b2b-seo.seo_title: On-Page SEO Case Study: Moroccan B2B Website

gallery_alts.0: Google Search Console: last 3 months compared with the previous 3 months

moroccan-b2b-seo.context: The client is a B2B company in Morocco that I worked with as a freelance consultant. Its pages were built and online, but they brought almost no traffic. The homepage appeared in Google, with about 4,330 impressions over three months, but it ranked too low and its search result was not convincing enough to earn clicks.

problems.title: The wrong keywords
problems.desc: Search Console data showed the pages were aimed at keywords that did not match what their potential clients searched for.

problems.title: Ranked too low
problems.desc: The homepage's average position was 34.2, on the fourth page of results, where very few people look.

problems.title: A search result people did not click
problems.desc: The click-through rate was 0.7%: out of every 1,000 times the page appeared, about 7 people clicked.

steps.title: Search Console analysis
steps.desc: I listed the pages and keywords with high impressions but poor positions: the searches where Google already showed the site but did not rank it well.

steps.title: Keyword and competitor research
steps.desc: Using Google Keyword Planner, Semrush and other tools, and by studying the competitors that ranked, I chose the keywords each page should target.

steps.title: Titles and descriptions rewritten
steps.desc: I rewrote the meta titles and descriptions to match search intent, so the result in Google gives people a reason to click.

steps.title: Content, internal links and schema
steps.desc: I made the pages clearer, strengthened the internal links and added schema markup so Google understands the business and its pages.

lessons: Impressions barely moved (+3.7%), but clicks more than doubled. The growth came from ranking higher and from a better search result, not from more visibility.
Before creating new pages, check the ones you have. Pages that already get impressions are often the fastest win.
The title and description are your ad in Google. Rewriting them around what people search for is one of the cheapest ways to raise clicks.

local-seo-guide-businesses.title: The Complete Local SEO Guide for Service Businesses
local-seo-guide-businesses.excerpt: A practical guide to Google Business Profile, local keywords and reviews, so nearby customers find you first.
local-seo-guide-businesses.content:
By Mohamed Toudghi – SEO & Digital Marketing Specialist

If you run a service-based business and want more customers from Google Search and Google Maps, Local SEO is one of the highest-ROI channels you can invest in.

Whether you’re a clinic, a restaurant, a real estate agency, or a service provider, your potential customers are already searching for you online.

This guide will show you, step by step, how to improve local SEO so you can rank higher, generate more leads, and build a trusted reputation. I’ll focus on practical tactics, backed by data, that work for businesses in any local market.

1. Why Local SEO Matters

Local search is no longer just “nice to have”. It’s how people make real buying decisions. If you’re not visible in Google’s Local Pack (the 3–4 map results) or in Maps, you’re losing customers to competitors who are.

2. How Google Local Search Works

Google’s local algorithm is based on three main factors: Proximity, Relevance, and Prominence.

3. Google Business Profile Optimization

Choose one primary category and relevant secondary categories. Avoid irrelevant ones. Regularly upload high-quality images of your team, office, and projects.

4. Local Keyword Research

Target patterns like [Service] + [City]. Language intent matters depending on your target audience.

5. On-Page Local SEO Optimization

  • Location Pages: Create dedicated pages for each city you serve.
  • Title Tags & Meta Descriptions: Include the main service and city name.

6. Local Citations & NAP Consistency

Ensure your Name, Address, and Phone (NAP) are consistent across all platforms.

7. Reviews & Local Trust Signals

Reviews are a core reputation signal. Respond professionally to all feedback.

8. Technical SEO for Local Rankings

Website speed and mobile-friendliness are essential. Implement LocalBusiness Schema Markup.

9. Final Action Plan & Checklist

  • ☐ Claim and verify your Google Business Profile
  • ☐ Standardize your NAP format across the web
  • ☐ Create dedicated city location pages
  • ☐ Implement a review collection process

By following this roadmap, you'll attract more leads and grow your business organically.

why-websites-fail.title: Why Most Websites Fail to Rank on Google (And How to Fix It)
why-websites-fail.excerpt: It's not just about keywords. It's about authority, user experience, and intent.
why-websites-fail.content: Websites often fail to rank not because of a single error, but due to a misalignment between content and search intent. If your page targets a high-volume keyword but doesn't answer the user's specific query, Google will prioritize more relevant competitors. Furthermore, authority is built through consistent, quality backlinks and internal linking structures that demonstrate topical expertise. Ensure your site is technically sound, but never forget that user experience and high-quality, helpful content are the ultimate drivers of search success.

ga4-event-tracking.title: GA4 Event Tracking for Service Websites
ga4-event-tracking.excerpt: How GA4 events work, which ones a service business should track (forms, calls, WhatsApp) and how to set them up with Google Tag Manager.
ga4-event-tracking.content: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) marks a major shift from session-based to event-based tracking. To get the most out of your data, you must move beyond simple pageview metrics. Start by defining your core conversion events, such as form submissions, button clicks, or video views. Use Google Tag Manager to implement these events without modifying code directly. By visualizing your conversion funnel in GA4 Explorations, you can identify precisely where users are dropping off and optimize your site for better performance.

keyword-research-process.title: My 4-Step Keyword Research Process
keyword-research-process.excerpt: How I find low-competition, high-value keywords for any niche.
keyword-research-process.content: Effective keyword research is about finding the intersection of volume, relevance, and difficulty. My 4-step process begins with seed keyword brainstorming based on core business services. Second, I use tools like SEMrush or Ahrefs to analyze competitor rankings and identify 'low-hanging fruit', keywords where competitors are weak. Third, I analyze the SERP intent to ensure we're creating the right type of content (informational vs transactional). Finally, I map these keywords to a content cluster strategy to build topical authority over time.

technical-seo-audit.lead: Google can only rank the pages it can crawl, render and index. I audit your whole site, find what blocks that, and hand you a clear plan ranked by its impact on traffic and leads.

definition.title: What is a technical SEO audit?
paragraphs: A technical SEO audit is a full check of the parts of a website that search engines rely on before they even read the content: crawling, rendering, indexing, site structure, page speed and structured data. It answers one question: can Google reach, understand and trust every page that matters to your business?

A content audit asks whether your pages say the right things. A technical audit asks whether Google can see them at all. When the technical base is broken, new content and new links are wasted, because the pages they point to never get indexed or load too slowly to rank.

For a service business or a SaaS company, the pages that matter are the ones that bring leads: service pages, location pages, pricing, demo and trial pages. My audit starts from those pages and works outwards.

for_who.title: When your site needs a technical SEO audit
items: Your pages do not show up in Google, or show up and then disappear.
Search Console lists pages as “Crawled, currently not indexed” or “Duplicate”.
Your site is slow on mobile or fails Core Web Vitals.
You redesigned or moved the site and traffic dropped.
You want an expert check before you spend more on content or ads.

included.title: What the technical SEO audit includes
included.intro: Every audit covers the same five areas. Each finding comes with the affected URLs, why it matters and how to fix it.

items.name: Full website crawl & technical error analysis
items.desc: I crawl every URL the way Googlebot does and list broken links, redirect chains, server errors, orphan pages and blocked resources.

items.name: Indexing, crawlability & canonical fixes
items.desc: I compare what you want indexed with what Google actually indexes, then fix robots.txt rules, noindex tags, canonical tags and sitemaps so the right version of each page ranks.

items.name: Core Web Vitals & performance recommendations
items.desc: I measure Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint and Cumulative Layout Shift on your real templates and list the changes that move them into the good range.

items.name: Schema & structured data implementation guidance
items.desc: I check your schema.org markup for errors and show which types fit your pages, such as Organization, Service, LocalBusiness, FAQPage or Article.

items.name: Internal linking & site architecture optimization
items.desc: I map how authority flows through your menus and links, find important pages buried too deep, and propose a structure where every service page sits close to the homepage.

compare.title: Technical SEO audit vs. full SEO audit
paragraphs: A full SEO audit covers three layers: technical health, content and keywords, and backlinks. A technical SEO audit goes deep on the first layer.

Start with the technical audit when pages are missing from Google, when traffic dropped after a redesign or migration, or when the site is slow. Once the base is solid, content and links finally have something to build on.

faqs.question: What does a technical SEO audit check?
faqs.answer: Everything that affects how Google crawls, indexes and ranks your pages: crawl errors and broken links, indexing and canonical tags, redirects, site structure and internal links, page speed and Core Web Vitals, mobile usability and structured data.

local-seo.lead: Show up when people nearby search for what you offer, in the Google map results and the local listings, and turn those searches into calls.

definition.title: What is local SEO?
paragraphs: Local SEO is the work of making a business visible when people search for a service in a specific place, such as “family lawyer Rabat” or “dentist near me”. Google answers these searches with a map, a short list of business profiles and then the regular results.

Google names three factors that decide who appears there: relevance (how well your profile and website match the search), distance (how close you are to the person searching) and prominence (how well known and trusted your business is, through reviews, links and citations). You cannot change your distance, so local SEO works on relevance and prominence.
For a service business, local search is often where the best leads come from: the person searching already knows what they need and is close enough to call today.

for_who.title: Signs your business needs local SEO
items: You do not appear in the map results for your main service in your city.
Competitors with fewer reviews rank above you.
Your business name, address or phone number differ from one directory to another.
You serve several cities but have one generic service page.
Calls and bookings from Google have slowed down.

items.name: Local landing page strategy

items.name: Review management framework

items.name: Local Map Pack visibility improvement

compare.title: Local SEO vs. traditional SEO
paragraphs: Traditional SEO competes for broad searches with no place in them, often against national websites. Local SEO competes for searches with a place, where your Google Business Profile, reviews and citations matter as much as your website.
Most service businesses need both: local SEO to win nearby customers, and a technically sound website so the service pages linked from the profile can rank and convert.

faqs.question: How long does local SEO take to show results?
faqs.answer: Fixes to your profile and citations can show in the map results within weeks. New pages and reviews build up over months. The pace depends on your city and your competition.

faqs.question: Do I need a website for local SEO?
faqs.answer: A Google Business Profile can rank on its own, but a website with a page for each service and city gives Google more reasons to trust you and gives visitors a place to convert.

faqs.question: How do reviews affect local rankings?
faqs.answer: Reviews are part of prominence. The number of reviews, the rating, how recent they are and whether you reply all help Google and customers trust your business.

faqs.question: Can you help if I serve several cities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each city and service combination usually needs its own useful page, linked from your profile and your main service pages.

ga4-tracking.lead: See which pages, searches and campaigns bring you leads, not only visits. I set up GA4 and Google Tag Manager properly and build a dashboard you will actually open.

definition.title: What is GA4 conversion tracking?
paragraphs: Google Analytics 4 (GA4) is Google's analytics platform. It records what visitors do on your website as events: a page view, a click on a phone number, a form submission. Conversion tracking means marking the events that create leads, so you can see exactly where those leads come from.
Google Tag Manager sends those events to GA4 and Google Ads without editing the website code each time. Looker Studio turns the data into a dashboard anyone on your team can read.
Without conversion tracking you see traffic but not results. With it, every page, keyword and campaign can be judged by the leads it brings.

You cannot tell which pages or campaigns bring form submissions, calls or WhatsApp messages.

Monthly reports take hours to put together.

compare.title: GA4 vs. Google Tag Manager
paragraphs: GA4 is where your data is stored and reported. Google Tag Manager is where tracking is configured and sent. You can run GA4 without Tag Manager, but every new event then needs a developer to edit the site.
Universal Analytics, the previous version of Google Analytics, stopped collecting data in July 2023, so GA4 is now the standard for every website.

faqs.question: Why use GA4 and Google Tag Manager together?
faqs.answer: GA4 stores and reports your data. Tag Manager is where the tracking lives, so events can be added or fixed without changing the website code each time.

faqs.question: Can you track WhatsApp and phone clicks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clicks on WhatsApp links, phone numbers and email addresses can be tracked as events and marked as conversions in GA4.

faqs.question: Does this work with Google Ads?
faqs.answer: Yes. GA4 conversions can be imported into Google Ads, so your campaigns are measured on real leads.

faqs.question: Can you fix an existing GA4 setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can review what is already in place, fix broken or duplicate events and clean up the reports.

faqs.question: How soon will I see data?
faqs.answer: Events start recording as soon as the setup is published. Useful trends appear after a few weeks of data.

faqs.question: How much does a GA4 setup cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on how many actions you want to track and how many sites or ad accounts are involved. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call.

seo-for-law-firms.title: SEO for law firms
seo-for-law-firms.lead: Get your firm found when people in your area search for a lawyer in your practice area, and turn those searches into consultations.

definition.title: What is law firm SEO?
paragraphs: Law firm SEO is the work of making a law firm appear in Google when someone searches for legal help, such as “personal injury lawyer Houston” or “divorce attorney near me”. Most of these searches name a practice area and a place, so law firm SEO is mostly local SEO applied to legal services.

Google answers these searches with ads, a map showing three firms, and then the regular results. The map depends on your Google Business Profile, your reviews and your distance from the person searching. The regular results depend on your website: one strong page per practice area and per city, a fast site, and links from trusted local and legal sources.

Legal searches are competitive because one client can be worth a lot to a firm. That is why structure matters more than volume: a clear site where each practice area has its own page does better than a large site where everything sits on one services page.

for_who.title: Signs your firm needs SEO work
items: Your firm does not appear in the map results for your main practice area in your city.
All your practice areas share one page, so none of them ranks well.
Directories list a different address or phone number for your firm.
Most new clients come from referrals or paid ads, and almost none from Google.
You serve several cities or counties with one generic page.

included.title: What law firm SEO work includes
included.intro: Six pieces of work, in the order that usually brings consultations fastest.

items.name: Practice area page structure
items.desc: One page per practice area, and per city where you have an office or serve clients. Each page explains the client's situation, what the firm does and how to get in touch. This is the structure behind the U.S. law firm case study below.

items.name: Google Business Profile for law firms
items.desc: The most precise primary category (for example “Personal injury attorney” rather than “Lawyer”), secondary categories for other practice areas, services, service area, photos and a description that follows Google's guidelines.

items.name: Legal and local citations
items.desc: Your firm's name, address and phone number made consistent across legal directories (Avvo, Justia, FindLaw, Martindale-Hubbell) and general ones (Yelp, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect).

items.name: Review routine
items.desc: A simple routine for asking satisfied clients for reviews and replying to each one, without revealing anything about the client's matter.

items.name: Technical and on-page fixes
items.desc: Titles and headings that name the practice area and the city, LegalService schema markup, fast mobile pages, and fixes for the indexing problems Search Console reports.

items.name: Lead tracking
items.desc: Calls, form submissions and consultation bookings tracked in GA4, so you know which practice area pages bring cases.

compare.title: Law firm SEO vs. Google Ads for lawyers
paragraphs: Google Ads puts your firm at the top of the page from the first day, and stops the day you stop paying. Legal keywords are among the most expensive in Google Ads, so each click can cost a firm a lot.

SEO takes months to build, but the rankings, reviews and pages keep bringing clients without a cost per click. Many firms use both: ads for immediate cases while SEO grows, then less ad spend as organic rankings take over.

faqs.question: How long does SEO take for a law firm?
faqs.answer: Fixes to your Google Business Profile and citations can show in the map results within weeks. Practice area pages and reviews build up over months. The pace depends on your city and how many firms compete for your practice area.

faqs.question: Which practice areas can you help with?
faqs.answer: Any practice area where clients search locally, such as personal injury, family law, immigration, criminal defense, estate planning or business law.

faqs.question: Do lawyer advertising rules affect SEO?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bar rules on lawyer advertising apply to your website, your profile and your review replies. Pages should not promise case outcomes, and replies to reviews should never reveal client information. Check your state bar's rules before publishing case results or testimonials.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate page for each city?
faqs.answer: If you have an office in that city or regularly serve clients there, yes. Each page needs real local details, not the same text with the city name changed.

faqs.question: How much does SEO for a law firm cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on how many practice areas and locations you have. You get a quote after the free 15-minute call, before any work starts.

faqs.question: Do you work with law firms outside the U.S.?
faqs.answer: Yes. I am based in Morocco, work remotely, and work with businesses in Morocco, the UK and the U.S., in English, French or Arabic.

definition.title: What an SEO consultant in Morocco does
paragraphs: An SEO consultant improves how a website appears in Google's organic results, the ones you do not pay for per click. In practice, that means finding what stops Google from crawling, understanding and ranking your pages, fixing it, and then measuring the effect on clicks, calls and enquiries.

In Morocco, this work has its own features: searches in French, Arabic and sometimes Darija, strong competition in the big cities, and customers who often contact businesses by phone or WhatsApp rather than through a form. An SEO strategy for the Moroccan market has to take all of this into account.

My name is Mohamed Toudghi. I am an independent SEO consultant based in Morocco and a graduate of Al Akhawayn University. I work with businesses in Morocco, the UK and the U.S., in three areas: technical SEO audits, local SEO and GA4 tracking.

proof.title: A measured result on a Moroccan website
proof.intro: A Moroccan B2B website got impressions on Google but very few clicks. Without adding new pages, I reworked the homepage keyword targeting, rewrote the titles and descriptions, and strengthened the internal links.
proof.source: Moroccan B2B website, Google Search Console data

market.title: SEO in Morocco: what is different
market.intro: Google's rules are the same everywhere, but the way people in Morocco search is not. Five points to handle from the start.

items.name: Three languages, sometimes four
items.desc: The same customer may search “avocat Casablanca”, “محامي الدار البيضاء” or type in Darija. A French-only website misses part of these searches. Each language needs its own pages, linked with hreflang tags, not a machine translation.

items.name: Local search, city by city
items.desc: For a law firm, a clinic or an agency, the Google map results (the Local Pack) often bring the best leads. They depend on a complete Google Business Profile, recent reviews and a page for each city you serve.

items.name: Mobile first
items.desc: Most local searches happen on a phone, often on a mobile connection. A slow website loses visitors before it shows what it offers. Mobile speed (Core Web Vitals) can be measured and fixed.

items.name: WhatsApp and phone calls as conversions
items.desc: Many customers in Morocco call or send a WhatsApp message instead of filling in a form. If those clicks are not tracked in GA4, you cannot tell which pages bring you customers.

items.name: .ma or .com domain
items.desc: A .ma domain tells Google the site targets Morocco, which helps a business that only sells in Morocco. If you also target Europe, Africa or the Gulf, a .com with one version per language is more flexible. Changing domain later needs a careful migration.

faqs.question: How much does an SEO consultant in Morocco cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the size of the site, the number of languages and cities, and the work needed: a one-off audit does not cost the same as several months of ongoing work. You get a precise quote after the free 15-minute call, before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see results?
faqs.answer: Technical fixes and Google Business Profile work can have an effect within weeks. For the Moroccan B2B website on this page, clicks grew by 130% in three months. Very competitive keywords usually take several months.

faqs.question: Do you work with businesses outside Casablanca?
faqs.answer: Yes. I work remotely with businesses in every Moroccan city, and also in the UK and the U.S.

faqs.question: Can you optimize a website in Arabic and French?
faqs.answer: Yes. I work in Arabic, French and English. On a multilingual website, each language has its own pages and keywords, linked with hreflang tags so Google shows each visitor the right version.

faqs.question: Do I need a .ma domain to rank in Morocco?
faqs.answer: No, but it helps if you only target Morocco. A .com can also rank in Morocco with local content, a Google Business Profile and links from Moroccan websites. The choice depends mostly on your markets abroad.

faqs.question: What is the difference between SEO and Google Ads?
faqs.answer: Google Ads shows your site at the top of the page as long as you pay for each click. SEO works on the organic results: it takes longer, but the rankings you earn keep bringing visits with no cost per click.

faqs.question: Do you work on WordPress, Shopify or custom websites?
faqs.answer: Yes, including WordPress (Elementor) and Shopify. On a custom website, I make the fixes myself or hand them to your developer with clear instructions.

faqs.question: How does the first contact work?
faqs.answer: You write to me through the form or on WhatsApp, or book a free 15-minute call. On the call we talk about your website, your goals and what can be improved. I reply within 24 hours.
